the surface charge of silicon surface barrier radiation detectors with a thin native oxide layer has an effect on the detector characteristics.

the effect of the surface charge and oxide layer thickness on the characteristics of the detectors.
the study of the influence of the surface charge on the detector's parameters and the application of silicon detectors for the detection of nuclear resonance reactions.
the development of silicon detectors with a nanoscale native oxide layer for nuclear resonance reaction measurements.

the oxide layer thickness is not a critical parameter in the design of silicon detectors for nuclear radiation detection.
the surface oxide layer is not the only reason for the degradation of the detector performance.

the oxide layer of a detector is a barrier for the charge carriers, which is a necessary condition for the operation of a detector.

the surface charge is a very important parameter for the operation of silicon surface barrier nuclear radiation detector.

the oxide layer should be as thick as possible to avoid the effect of surface charge on the detector's characteristics.
